text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: kvcache-hosted OOM rate spike detected on prod-runtime-gpu-*. Alerting on-call.

maya (oncall): Seeing a flurry of OOMs and 500s on hosted runtime. Likely tied to large-context requests. Triage?

ryan: Confirmed. Spikes started ~1723459900. Error pattern: `kvcache: alloc failed` then eviction thrash. Continuous batching backlog grows.

anya: Any recent rollout of batching config or prefetch heuristics? I rolled a minor batch-size clamp yesterday but it was small.

jess (eng-runtime): We did deploy a kvmap prefetch change 6h ago that widened prefetch window for long prompts. Could cause orphaned keys and mem retention. Reverting candidate: rollback prefetched-window to 512 -> 256.

maya (oncall): Support reports some customers seeing elevated latency and 502/500s. Need emergency mitigation to reduce blast radius.

support-bot: Two enterprise tenants (cust-421, cust-779) reported failed generations and session timeouts. ETA impact: intermittent since 10:05UTC.

sre-lead: Immediate mitigations: 1) disable aggressive prefetch via hotpatch 2) reduce max_batch_time from 50ms -> 20ms 3) increase kv eviction pressure (lower threshold). Which one is fastest?

jess (eng-runtime): Fastest is flipping the prefetch flag. Hotpatch command below. Will push with deploy-bot if approved.

```
# hotpatch: runtime config
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/configs/hotpatch \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"kvcache.prefetch.enabled":false}'
```

maya (oncall): Do it. I'll monitor memory and errors. @deploy-bot, trigger hotpatch. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Hotpatch queued by maya (oncall). Rolling to runtimes in parallel (5s stagger).

ryan: Patch applied to 3 clusters. Memory trends flattening on two; one still climbing (prod-runtime-gpu-7).

jess (eng-runtime): If memory doesn't fall, we can trigger an immediate per-host KV eviction sweep: `kvcachectl evict --age 1m --force` (risky for perf). Hold unless needed.

maya (oncall): Hold. Watching. Support, notify customers cust-421 and cust-779 that we're mitigating and monitoring.

support-bot: Notified both customers with interim message and status page update.

ryan: prod-runtime-gpu-7 memory plateaued and started declining after patch. Error rate down ~85% from peak. Latency normalizing.

jess (eng-runtime): We'll follow up with a small rollback of the prefetch widen change in main branch and schedule a canary for less permissive prefetch thresholds. Also add limit on per-session prefetched tokens.

maya (oncall): Oncall handoff in 40m. I'll leave a brief note: resolved by disabling prefetch. Watch for reappearance after rollback.

sre-lead: Postmortem items: 1) Add automatic circuit-breaker when kvcache alloc rate per-node exceeds threshold 2) Add tighter canary for prefetch rollouts 3) Add per-customer sampling to avoid single-tenant large-context blasts.

jess (eng-runtime): I'll open PRs for 1 and 2. Also adding metric kvcache.prefetch_orphans_count.

maya (oncall): Thanks all. Handing off to ryan for the overnight watch. ryan, you're oncall until 1723493599.

ryan: Ack. I'll keep monitoring and escalate if anything recurs.

incident-bot: Incident tagged: kvcache-long-context-prefetch->mitigated. Severity: Sev2.

maya (oncall): Quick customer impact summary for postmortem: two enterprise tenants saw intermittent 5xxs and timeouts for ~25 minutes; no data loss; mitigation applied via hotpatch disabling prefetch; subsequent rollback planned to avoid recurrence.

support-bot: Saved incident notes and customer comms draft to /incidents/1723459999/notes.

jess (eng-runtime): Locking the prefetched-window rollout until design review complete.

maya (oncall): Closing thread but will add final timeline later. Good job everyone. :heart:
